title: Serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonist
abstract:
Many serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor agonists, due to lack of selectivity and activation of the closely related serotonin 5-HT<sub>2B</sub> receptor, may have the potential to produce organ fibrosis and associated complications such as cardiac valvulopathy or pulmonary hypertension with long-term use. This has been observed with pharmaceutical drugs such as fenfluramine, methysergide, ergotamine, cabergoline, and pergolide, among others, which has led to market withdrawal or restrictions on use of such agents. Infrequent or occasional use of serotonergic psychedelics is thought to be safe and not pose a significant risk, but very frequent use or microdosing may carry risk. Not all serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor agonists are also potent serotonin 5-HT<sub>2B</sub> receptor agonists however. For example, many phenethylamine psychedelics show substantial selectivity for the serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> and 5-HT<sub>2C</sub> receptors over the serotonin 5-HT<sub>2B</sub> receptor. In addition, selective serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor agonists that show less or no activation of other serotonin receptors such as the serotonin 5-HT<sub>2B</sub> receptor, such as 25CN-NBOH, DMBMPP, LPH-5, and TGF-8027, have been developed. Moreover, selective serotonin 5-HT<sub>2B</sub> receptor antagonists, including peripherally selective drugs like VU0530244, are being developed, and may be able to block the complications of serotonin 5-HT<sub>2B</sub> receptor agonism.
### 5-HT2A receptor agonists and neurotoxicity  
Serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor agonists may produce neurotoxicity, for instance serotonergic neurotoxicity, at high concentrations or doses. In addition, they may potentiate the serotonergic neurotoxicity of MDMA.
## Indirect 5-HT2A receptor agonists  
Serotonergic agents that elevate serotonin levels can act as indirect serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor agonists. Examples of such agents include serotonin precursors like tryptophan and 5-hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP), serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SRIs) like selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and various other antidepressants, monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), and serotonin releasing agents (SRAs) like fenfluramine and MDMA. Direct serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor agonists and serotonin-elevating drugs have differing effects. As an example, whereas serotonin-elevating drugs have a risk of serotonin syndrome, major serotonergic psychedelics like psilocybin and LSD are partial agonists of the serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor and have little or no risk of serotonin syndrome even in the context of large overdoses. However, one notable group of psychedelics, the NBOMe drugs, have higher efficacy at the serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor and can produce serotonin syndrome. As another example, serotonin is a highly hydrophilic molecule and is unable to enter neurons and activate intracellular serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptors, which have been found to mediate the psychoplastogenic effects of exogenous serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor agonists. These intracellular serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptors may also contribute to the psychedelic effects of serotonin 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor agonists.
